chunks: And Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding the mahsūr who did not bring the sacrificial animal, he said: “He performs his rites and returns.”
It was said: “Then if he does not find a sacrificial animal?” He said: “He fasts.”

key_terms.هَدْيًا: a sacrificial offering in the context of pilgrimage
key_terms.يَرْجِعُ: he returns after carrying out the required ruling
key_terms.يَصُومُ: he fasts as a substitute when the offering is unavailable
key_terms.يَنْسُكُ: he performs the ritual act or rite required of him
key_terms.ٱلْمَحْصُورِ: a pilgrim prevented or restricted from completing the hajj or ʿumrah rites
key_terms.ٱلْهَدْيَ: the sacrificial animal offered in connection with pilgrimage rites

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a mahsur who did not bring or cannot find a sacrificial animal?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the mahsūr, one prevented from completing the rites, when he has not brought a sacrificial animal. The Imam عليه السلام states that he performs the required rite and returns, and if he cannot find a sacrificial animal, he fasts instead.
